title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, jam/spoof triage, fallback recommendation) with a formation-level PNT interference picture feeding the C2/EW COP
version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION per G04-score.json (verdict: borderline). This plan is designed ONLY for the vendor-neutral composite-assurance engine: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant plug-in that ingests 3-8 heterogeneous PNT sources, emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, explainable fault/jam/spoof classification and a fallback recommendation, plus a synthetic scenario generator and a replay/audit library validated against public recordings (TEXBAT-type) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 behaviors. It is NOT designed for the single-pane HMI as the product (a thin demo HMI is only a window onto the engine) and NOT for the formation-level PNT interference picture / EW COP feed (killed in the score file as classified-adjacent and NGC2-absorbable). Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt from the score file: does a named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for this software layer, and can this founding team lawfully reach it? Honest framing: until a Phase II/OT or Phase III appears, this is a credibility-and-evidence path with SBIR-scale money (single-digit $M), not yet a venture-scale company.

links.value: Shipboard navigation watchstanders monitor several fragmented GPS/INS/GPNTS/alternate-source displays and must manually infer hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing and pick a fallback, with no composite confidence, explainable rationale or audit trail.
links.detail: FACT: Navy CSO open topic DON26BX05-NP004 text and Q&A state operators 'interact with multiple interfaces and data sources', that this 'fragmented environment increases cognitive workload... and slows decision-making', and that success metrics are speed to decision during an anomaly, threat comprehension accuracy and correct fallback selection (topic posted 2026-08-05; Q&A 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01, read via mirror in the G04 card). OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) (2019-09-30) has required operator degradation indication and interference reporting to electronic support since 2019.

money_map.weakest_link: BUDGET (and, tied to it, CONTRACT VEHICLE). The buyer chain from problem to program office is now verified end-to-end - PMW/A 170 exists, owns GPNTS, and has bought PNT situational-awareness software at SBIR scale twice (2024/2025 BlueRISC, 2026 NP004) - but no program budget line, Phase III, ECP or production award for this software layer is evidenced; the only open vehicle closed on 2026-09-23; and the sole path into the fielded system runs through Raytheon's software-support IDIQ, which the founders cannot access directly.
money_map.penalty_note: Major penalty retained from the score file. Evidenced money is SBIR caps plus one $750K Phase II; IDIQ ceilings ($452.85M hardware) must not be read as software demand; a prototype award (BlueRISC Phase II) is not deployment; and the pattern Phase I -> Phase II -> new open topic without a production step is the proto-purgatory GAO described. The plan below is therefore structured to produce evidence quickly and to kill quickly: if no named PMW 170 or NP004-awardee counterpart engages by week 12, and no second vehicle (IWRP/CRADA/D2P2/civil pilot) is in motion by month 9, the company should not raise venture money on this opportunity.

questions: Walk me through the last time you saw a GPS or navigation-source anomaly on watch: what did you see first, on which display, and what did you do in the first 60 seconds?
Which indicators did you actually look at to decide whether it was a hardware fault, jamming or spoofing, and in what order? What did you ignore?
How did you decide which fallback to use (alternate source, INS-only, celestial/radar/DR), and who had to agree before you shifted?
What did you write in the navigation workbook or report afterwards, and who, if anyone, received the interference information (EW cell, IWC, NAVCEN, fleet)?
Show me, on a whiteboard, every display and panel you monitor during a contested-strait transit and which system each belongs to.
When GPNTS or a receiver reports 'degraded', how much do you trust it, and what have you seen it get wrong?
Tell me about a time the team disagreed about whether you were being spoofed; how was it resolved and how long did it take?
If you had to explain to the CO after the fact why you shifted sources at 0213, what evidence would you want to be able to pull up?
How were you trained on jam/spoof triage, and what parts of the training did not match what you saw at sea?
For the program-office and engineering roles: walk me through how a new software capability gets onto GPNTS today, from idea to fleet install, and where it usually stalls.
What did the last GPNTS situational-awareness effort deliver, and what would you need to see from a vendor-neutral assurance component before you would let it sit under your display?
For the pntOS/ASPN roles: walk me through how a third-party plug-in is accepted into the ecosystem and tested, and what integrity or assurance messages you wish plug-ins emitted.
For commercial masters: walk me through your last GPS-disruption transit, what your company's disruption plan told you to do, and what you actually reported to NAVCEN or your DPA.
Which of your current tools or vendors would you expect to add this kind of composite confidence next, and why haven't they?
What would make you stop trusting an automated fallback recommendation, and what would it take to earn that trust back?

first_deployment_path.path: Two-track. Track A (government, evidence): become the assurance-engine component inside an NP004 Phase I awardee's prototype (or inside the incumbent SBIR vendor's follow-on) so that the engine runs on GPNTS-furnished ICD data in their Phase I/II, then demonstrate it at an ANTX/NICE event or JNC 2027 and, through an NIWC Pacific CRADA, on a NIWC lab GPNTS string. Track B (paying, unclassified): a pilot on 2-5 commercial vessels of one operator with routine Red Sea/Baltic transits (or one allied navy training/hydrographic vessel), consuming NMEA/IEC 61162 receiver telemetry plus INS, running the same engine air-gapped on bridge hardware, producing real interference recordings and audit logs. Track B is the first deployment the founders control; Track A is the one the Navy will credit.
first_deployment_path.evidence_it_produces: For a Navy Phase II/D2P2 or OT: measured detection latency, classification accuracy and false-alert rate on both synthetic and real recordings; an operator study against the Navy's own NP004 metrics (speed to decision, threat comprehension accuracy, correct fallback selection) with former ETVs/QMs; a conformant ASPN/pntOS plug-in exercised on a lab GPNTS string (CRADA); a demonstration record at ANTX/JNC. For a seed/Series A or STRATFI-equivalent (Navy has no branded STRATFI; analog is Phase II sequential/enhancement funding): one paying pilot with renewal, a government-funded Phase II or OT (or a subcontract on one), a named transition owner in PMW 170, and a counsel-cleared U.S.-person-controlled cap table. For DIU-style production: a fielded pilot on a government platform with an ATO path (RAISE/OSA container) - not reachable inside 12 months by public evidence.
alternatives: Army route: pntOS plug-in accepted by C5ISR Center and run at PNTAX (annual, WSMR) under a government sponsor - requires a sponsor and U.S.-person staff for threat data; longer path, larger fleet of MAPS/DAPS hosts.
Prime's demo: offer the engine to Raytheon's GPNTS software support team as a candidate ECP component; yields ICD access but risks becoming a work-for-hire feature with no data rights.

NATO DIANA 2026/2027 cohort (Electromagnetic Resilience / Data-Assisted Decision Making challenges; 150 companies selected from 3,600+ in 2026) - allied test-centre access and a non-U.S. funding line; German entity may be required.
DHS/CISA critical-infrastructure timing pilot under the Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 - civil, unclassified, but a different product variant (cloud-tolerant, single-receiver).

allied_extension.bigger_with_allies: Moderately bigger and materially de-risking, but not transformative in evidenced dollars. Allies face harsher real-world interference (Baltic, Black Sea, Eastern Mediterranean, Red Sea) and have no citizenship gate on an unclassified, EAR-only engine; NATO DIANA explicitly solicits 'Electromagnetic Resilience' (sensing, navigation, data link in contested EMS) and 'Data-Assisted Decision Making' (E06-F1, 2026 cohort); Project Overmatch's Five Eyes arrangement gives a coalition C2 context; and the German founder's network is a real asset in Germany. No allied program of record for a PNT awareness/decision layer was verified this session - Public evidence insufficient - so allied demand is INFERENCE/MEDIUM, and allied revenue is plausible only for the unclassified operator/assurance layer, never for aggregated threat pictures (DoDI 4650.08 transfer limits; coalition releasability unresolved).
allied_extension.what_changes: (1) Product must stay EAR-only and vendor-neutral (public ASPN YAML, NMEA/IEC 61162, S-52/BAM-compatible outputs) with no U.S.-CUI-derived signatures in the allied build - two code trains (U.S. CUI build vs releasable build) from day one. (2) Corporate structure: a U.S. Inc. for DoD plus a possible German GmbH for EDF/DIANA/Bundeswehr work; E06-F38 says single-jurisdiction structuring is lossy in every direction and counsel must map ITAR deemed-export, EDF/EDIP control and German clearance rules against the first customer. (3) Interfaces multiply: each navy runs different fusion engines and ECDIS suppliers, so the ASPN plug-in plus a small adapter set is the only scalable form. (4) Evidence base improves: allied and commercial recordings of real interference feed the scenario library, which is the moat. (5) Timing: DIANA application windows are annual; JNC 2027 and European Navigation Conference are the venues.

most_important_question.build_first: Build the assurance engine, not the screen: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant integrity service, packaged as an air-gapped OCI container, that consumes a synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (3-8 sources at 1-10 Hz: GNSS jamming onset, spoofing pull-off, INS drift, clock holdover, hardware fault) and emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, an explainable fault/jam/spoof classification, a fallback recommendation with rationale, and a replayable audit timeline - validated against held-out synthetic scenarios, public real recordings (TEXBAT-type) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 Respond/Recover behaviors. Add a thin ECDIS-style demo HMI only as a window onto the engine, and publish a reference plug-in subset to the Open-PNT community so the engine becomes the thing others plug into. Budget: roughly $80K over 90 days and $100-150K over 4-5 months, within founder capital.
most_important_question.show_it_to: In order: (1) NP004 Phase I awardees as soon as selections post (~Q1-Q2 2027) and the incumbent SBIR vendor (BlueRISC, whose $750K GPNTS SA Tool Phase II ended 2026-05-25) - as a component supplier; (2) the PMW/A 170 GPNTS office (NP004 TPOC via the NAVWAR Small Business Office) and the NIWC Pacific GPNTS/Raytheon software-support engineers - as the candidate for the next open-topic cycle, a D2P2 or a GPNTS ECP, via a CRADA; (3) the Open-PNT / ISTO ASPN community and Army C5ISR Center pntOS engineers - as a reference plug-in; (4) one commercial operator with Red Sea/Baltic transits or one allied navy officer - as an unclassified paid pilot; (5) JNC 2027 (2027-06-07 to 06-10, Covington KY) as the single public venue where all of the above are in one room.
most_important_question.demo_proves: Against the Navy's own NP004 metrics: detection latency under 1 s at 1-10 Hz; correct fault/jam/spoof classification on held-out synthetic and public real recordings with a quantified false-alert rate (targets: >=90% classification accuracy on synthetic, >=80% on public real recordings, <5% false alerts); former watchstanders reach the correct fallback measurably faster and with fewer errors than with fragmented displays (n>=6 operator study); every recommendation carries an evidence chain and can be replayed for after-action review; and the same container consumes an ASPN/pntOS stream unchanged, so a Phase II can swap in GPNTS ICDs without rework.
most_important_question.why_customer_cares: PMW 170 wrote the problem in its own words (NP004, 2026-08-05) and has now paid for PNT situational-awareness software at least twice (2024 Phase I, 2025 Phase II $750K) and re-solicited it more broadly in 2026 with multiple awards planned, so it is not satisfied with what it has; OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) has required degradation indication and interference reporting since 2019 and systems that cannot comply must seek waivers; the GPNTS software-support ceiling was exhausted early by 'emergent fleet needs'; GPS denial is routine (12 DoD interference tests in Aug-Sep 2026 per NAVCEN; MARAD 2026-008 global advisory) and M-code remains late in all three segments (GAO-24-106841, 2024-09-09); and every Phase I awardee will need validated assurance analytics they do not have.
most_important_question.why_incumbent_cant_crush: Honestly, this is a speed-and-evidence defense, not a structural one, which is why the verdict is borderline. What protects the founders: receiver primes (Collins, BAE, L3Harris, Safran) have no incentive to ship vendor-neutral assurance that commoditizes their boxes; Raytheon as GPNTS prime is a systems house on a ceiling-exhausted support contract and has not fielded this layer in seven years; BlueRISC's effort is an AI/ML module tied to GPNTS rather than an open ASPN/pntOS-conformant engine with a scenario/replay library; NGC2/Overmatch integrators lack PNT-integrity depth; and IS4S - the one competitor who could build this - is committed to Army NorthStar (up to $41M, April 2026) and AF design-agent work and may prefer to license a validated component. The founders lose if they build a dashboard; they can hold only if the validated algorithms, the scenario/replay library with real recordings from civil/allied pilots, the operator-study evidence and conformance to open standards make them the reference implementation everyone else plugs in.
most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m: All four within 18 months, or stop: (1) a funded Navy Phase II, D2P2 or OT - or a paid subcontract on one - with GPNTS ICDs in hand and a scheduled fleet, ANTX or PNTAX demonstration; (2) at least one paying unclassified civil or allied pilot with a renewal; (3) a named PMW 170 transition owner and a documented path (ECP, RAISE/OSA container, or Phase III) into GPNTS or pntOS; (4) a counsel-cleared U.S.-person-controlled cap table plus a CMMC Level 2 self-assessment and a CUI enclave. If, at 18 months, the only money is Phase I-scale and the government has taken the layer GOTS or bought it from the standard-setter, the founders should stop - this opportunity's evidenced money is single-digit millions and a $2-5M raise is justified only by a transition owner with a vehicle, not by prototypes.
